items.informal_name: Hasse Derivative of Monomial in Polynomial Ring
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : Semiring R] (k n : ℕ) (r : R),
  (Polynomial.hasseDeriv k) ((Polynomial.monomial n) r) = (Polynomial.monomial (n - k)) (↑(n.choose k) * r)
items.informal_description: For a semiring $ R $, the $ k $-th Hasse derivative of the monomial $ rX^n $ in the polynomial ring $ R[X] $ is given by $ \binom{n}{k} r X^{n - k} $. This expresses how the Hasse derivative acts on monomials by scaling the coefficient by the binomial coefficient $ \binom{n}{k} $ and reducing the degree by $ k $.

items.informal_name: Partial Derivative of Monomial: $\partial_i (a X^s) = a s_i X^{s - e_i}$
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u} {σ : Type v} {a : R} {s : σ →₀ ℕ} [inst : CommSemiring R] {i : σ},
  (MvPolynomial.pderiv i) ((MvPolynomial.monomial s) a) = (MvPolynomial.monomial (s - Finsupp.single i 1)) (a * ↑(s i))
items.informal_description: For a commutative semiring $ R $, a type $ \sigma $, and a monomial $ a X^s $ in the multivariate polynomial ring $ R[\sigma] $, the partial derivative with respect to the variable indexed by $ i \in \sigma $ is the monomial with coefficient $ a \cdot s(i) $ and exponent vector $ s - \mathbf{e}_i $, where $ \mathbf{e}_i $ denotes the standard basis vector with 1 at position $ i $ and 0 elsewhere.

items.informal_name: Hasse Derivative of Order k Applied to a Polynomial
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : Semiring R] (k : ℕ) (f : Polynomial R),
  (Polynomial.hasseDeriv k) f = f.sum fun i r => (Polynomial.monomial (i - k)) (↑(i.choose k) * r)
items.informal_description: For a semiring $ R $ and a polynomial $ f \in R[X] $, the Hasse derivative of order $ k $ applied to $ f $ is given by $ D^{(k)}(f) = \sum_{i} \binom{i}{k} \cdot a_i \cdot X^{i - k} $, where $ a_i $ is the coefficient of $ X^i $ in $ f $. This expression sums over all monomials in $ f $, scaling each by the binomial coefficient $ \binom{i}{k} $ and reducing the exponent by $ k $.

items.informal_name: Derivation of Monomials in Multivariate Polynomial Ring
items.type:
∀ {σ : Type u_1} (R : Type u_2) {A : Type u_3} [inst : CommSemiring R] [inst_1 : AddCommMonoid A] [inst_2 : Module R A]
  [inst_3 : Module (MvPolynomial σ R) A] [inst_4 : IsScalarTower R (MvPolynomial σ R) A] (f : σ → A) (s : σ →₀ ℕ)
  (r : R),
  (MvPolynomial.mkDerivation R f) ((MvPolynomial.monomial s) r) =
    r • s.sum fun i k => (MvPolynomial.monomial (s - Finsupp.single i 1)) ↑k • f i
items.informal_description: For a commutative semiring $ R $, type $ \sigma $, $ R $-module $ A $, and function $ f : \sigma \to A $, the derivation $ D_f $ applied to the monomial $ r \cdot \mathbf{X}^s $ (where $ s : \sigma \to_0 \mathbb{N} $ and $ r \in R $) yields $ r \cdot \sum_{i \in \text{supp}(s)} \mathbf{X}^{s - \mathbf{e}_i} \cdot f(i) $. Here, $ \mathbf{e}_i $ denotes the basis vector with 1 at position $ i $, and $ \mathbf{X}^{s - \mathbf{e}_i} $ represents the monomial obtained by reducing the exponent of variable $ i $ by 1.

items.informal_name: Derivation on Multivariate Polynomial Monomials Induced by Function f
items.type:
∀ {σ : Type u_1} {R : Type u_2} {A : Type u_3} [inst : CommSemiring R] [inst_1 : AddCommMonoid A] [inst_2 : Module R A]
  [inst_3 : Module (MvPolynomial σ R) A] (f : σ → A) (s : σ →₀ ℕ) (r : R),
  (MvPolynomial.mkDerivationₗ R f) ((MvPolynomial.monomial s) r) =
    r • s.sum fun i k => (MvPolynomial.monomial (s - Finsupp.single i 1)) ↑k • f i
items.informal_description: For a commutative semiring $ R $, a type $ \sigma $ of variables, and a function $ f : \sigma \to A $, the derivation $ D $ induced by $ f $ acts on the monomial $ r \cdot X^s $ (where $ s : \sigma \to_0 \mathbb{N} $ and $ r \in R $) by producing the sum $ \sum_{i \in \text{supp}(s)} r \cdot f(i) \cdot X^{s - \mathbf{e}_i} $, where $ \mathbf{e}_i $ denotes the unit vector at $ i $. This satisfies the Leibniz rule for derivations.

items.informal_name: Partial Derivative of Monomial with Respect to Variable i Follows Power Rule
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u} {σ : Type v} {a : R} [inst : CommSemiring R] {i : σ} {n : ℕ},
  (MvPolynomial.pderiv i) ((MvPolynomial.monomial (Finsupp.single i n)) a) =
    (MvPolynomial.monomial (Finsupp.single i (n - 1))) (a * ↑n)
items.informal_description: For a commutative semiring $ R $, type $ \sigma $, variable $ i \in \sigma $, natural number $ n $, and coefficient $ a \in R $, the partial derivative of the monomial $ a \cdot X_i^n $ with respect to $ X_i $ is $ a \cdot n \cdot X_i^{n-1} $. This follows the standard power rule for differentiation in multivariate polynomial rings.

items.informal_name: Hasse Derivative of Order $ k $ Applied to Single-Term Laurent Series: $ \text{hasseDeriv}_k(\text{single}_n(x)) = \text{single}_{n - k}\left( \binom{n}{k} \cdot x \right) $
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : Semiring R] {V : Type u_2} [inst_1 : AddCommGroup V] [inst_2 : Module R V] (k : ℕ) (n : ℤ)
  (x : V), (LaurentSeries.hasseDeriv R k) ((HahnSeries.single n) x) = (HahnSeries.single (n - ↑k)) (Ring.choose n k • x)
items.informal_description: The Hasse derivative of order $ k $ applied to the Laurent series with a single non-zero term at exponent $ n $ and coefficient $ x $ results in a Laurent series with a single non-zero term at exponent $ n - k $, scaled by the binomial coefficient $ \binom{n}{k} $. Formally, $ \text{hasseDeriv}_k(\text{single}_n(x)) = \text{single}_{n - k}\left( \binom{n}{k} \cdot x \right) $.

items.type:

  ((Polynomial.hasseDeriv k) f).coeff n = ↑((n + k).choose k) * f.coeff (n + k)
items.informal_description: For any natural number $ n $, the coefficient of $ X^n $ in the $ k $-th Hasse derivative of a polynomial $ f $ over a semiring $ R $ is equal to $ \binom{n + k}{k} $ multiplied by the coefficient of $ X^{n + k} $ in $ f $.

items.informal_name: Hasse Derivative of a Single Laurent Series Term
items.type:

  (x : V),
  (LaurentSeries.hasseDeriv R k) ((HahnSeries.single (n + ↑k)) x) = (HahnSeries.single n) (Ring.choose (n + ↑k) k • x)
items.informal_description: The Hasse derivative of order $k$ applied to the Laurent series with a single non-zero term at exponent $n + k$ and coefficient $x$ results in the Laurent series with a single non-zero term at exponent $n$ and coefficient $\binom{n + k}{k} \cdot x$, where $\binom{n + k}{k}$ denotes the binomial coefficient in the ring $R$.

items.informal_name: Hasse Derivative of Order k on Polynomial Ring
items.type: {R : Type u_1} → [inst : Semiring R] → ℕ → Polynomial R →ₗ[R] Polynomial R
items.informal_description: For a semiring $ R $, the Hasse derivative of order $ k $ is an $ R $-linear map $ D^{(k)} : R[X] 	o R[X] $ defined by $ D^{(k)}(a_i X^i) =  inom{i}{k} a_i X^{i - k} $ on monomials and extended linearly. This operation generalizes the usual derivative by scaling each coefficient $ a_i $ by the binomial coefficient $  inom{i}{k} $ and reducing the degree by $ k $.

items.informal_name: Linear Sum Identity for Single-Nonzero Finite Support Functions
items.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {M : Type u_2} {N : Type u_3} {R : Type u_5} {R₂ : Type u_6} (S : Type u_8) [inst : Semiring R]
  [inst_1 : Semiring R₂] [inst_2 : Semiring S] [inst_3 : AddCommMonoid M] [inst_4 : Module R M]
  [inst_5 : AddCommMonoid N] [inst_6 : Module R₂ N] {σ : R →+* R₂} [inst_7 : Module S N] [inst_8 : SMulCommClass R₂ S N]
  (f : α → M →ₛₗ[σ] N) (i : α) (m : M), ((Finsupp.lsum S) f) (Finsupp.single i m) = (f i) m
items.informal_description: For any family of $\sigma$-linear maps $f : \alpha \to M \to_\sigma N$, index $i \in \alpha$, and element $m \in M$, the linear sum $\text{lsum} \, f$ evaluated at the finite support function $\text{single}_i(m)$ equals $f(i)(m)$.

items.informal_name: Linear Sum Evaluates to Component Map on Single-Element Insertion
items.type:
∀ {ι : Type u_1} {R : Type u_3} (S : Type u_4) {M : ι → Type u_5} {N : Type u_6} [inst : Semiring R]
  [inst_1 : (i : ι) → AddCommMonoid (M i)] [inst_2 : (i : ι) → Module R (M i)] [inst_3 : AddCommMonoid N]
  [inst_4 : Module R N] [inst_5 : DecidableEq ι] [inst_6 : Semiring S] [inst_7 : Module S N]
  [inst_8 : SMulCommClass R S N] (F : (i : ι) → M i →ₗ[R] N) (i : ι) (x : M i),
  ((DFinsupp.lsum S) F) (DFinsupp.single i x) = (F i) x
items.informal_description: For a semiring $ S $, family of $ S $-modules $ \{M(i)\}_{i \in \iota} $, and another $ S $-module $ N $, given a family of $ S $-linear maps $ F_i : M(i) \to N $, the linear map $ \Phi $ constructed by $ \mathrm{lsum} $ satisfies $ \Phi(\mathrm{single}_i(x)) = F_i(x) $ for any $ x \in M(i) $. This states that applying the linear sum map to a function with a single non-zero element $ x $ at index $ i $ yields the result of the $ i $-th component map applied to $ x $.

items.informal_name: Composition of Finsupp.lsum and lsingle Recovers Original Map
items.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {M : Type u_2} {N : Type u_3} {R : Type u_5} {R₂ : Type u_6} (S : Type u_8) [inst : Semiring R]
  [inst_1 : Semiring R₂] [inst_2 : Semiring S] [inst_3 : AddCommMonoid M] [inst_4 : Module R M]
  [inst_5 : AddCommMonoid N] [inst_6 : Module R₂ N] {σ : R →+* R₂} [inst_7 : Module S N] [inst_8 : SMulCommClass R₂ S N]
  (f : α → M →ₛₗ[σ] N) (i : α), (Finsupp.lsum S) f ∘ₛₗ Finsupp.lsingle i = f i
items.informal_description: For any family of σ-linear maps $ f: \alpha \to M \to_\sigma N $ and any index $ i \in \alpha $, the composition of the linear equivalence $ \text{Finsupp.lsum} \, f $ with the single-index embedding $ \text{lsingle}_i $ equals the map $ f(i) $. This establishes that applying the linear sum equivalence followed by the single-index embedding reconstructs the original map at index $ i $.

items.informal_name: Linear Combination of Single Index Vector
items.type:
∀ (α : Type u_1) (M : Type u_2) (R : Type u_5) [inst : Semiring R] [inst_1 : AddCommMonoid M] [inst_2 : Module R M]
  (c : M) (a : α) (f : α →₀ R) [inst_3 : DecidableEq α], (Finsupp.linearCombination R (Pi.single a c)) f = f a • c
items.informal_description: For any element $c$ in the module $M$, index $a$ in $\alpha$, and finite support function $f : \alpha \to_0 R$ with decidable equality on $\alpha$, the linear combination map evaluated at the function $\mathrm{single}_a(c)$ (which is $c$ at index $a$ and zero elsewhere) and $f$ yields the scalar multiplication of $f(a)$ with $c$, i.e., $\mathrm{linearCombination}_R(\mathrm{single}_a(c), f) = f(a) \cdot c$.

items.informal_name: Linear Combination of Single Term Equals Scalar Multiple
items.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {M : Type u_2} (R : Type u_5) [inst : Semiring R] [inst_1 : AddCommMonoid M] [inst_2 : Module R M]
  {v : α → M} (c : R) (a : α), (Finsupp.linearCombination R v) (Finsupp.single a c) = c • v a
items.informal_description: For any semiring $R$, index type $\alpha$, $R$-module $M$, and function $v : \alpha \to M$, the linear combination map applied to the finite support function with a single non-zero coefficient $c$ at index $a$ equals $c \cdot v(a)$.
